chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

'Shall I not inform you of Islam, its root, its branch, and the peak of its hump?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'As for its root, it is the Salat, and its branch is the Zakat, and the peak of its hump is the Jihad.'

Then he said: 'If you wish, I will inform you of the doors of goodness.' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said: 'The Sawm is a shield from the Fire, and the Sadaqah removes the mistakes, and the standing of the man in the depth of the night with the Dhikr of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the root, branch, and peak of Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) employs an organic metaphor to structure the pillars of Islam, positioning Salat as the foundational root, Zakat as the sustaining branch, and Jihad as the apex of spiritual elevation. He further elucidates the 'doors of goodness' by linking fasting to protection from Hellfire, charity to the expiation of sins, and night prayer (Qiyam) to divine remembrance, explicitly citing the virtue of those who pray in the depths of the night.
